audit.whatIsWrong: Row 2 (Level 3) read Skill in both layers while the packet chart says Sett and the page's own whys[2] says 'Level 3 E Facebreaker lets you pull her before she can center Mist' — a Sett-favoured sentence on a Skill row. The rest of the chart already agrees with the mirror (Levels 1-2 Sett, 4-5 Skill, Level 6 Gwen).
audit.why: Facebreaker comes online at 3 and Hallowed Mist is 22s at rank 1, so level 3 is the clearest Sett window in the lane. The mirror settled rows 0, 1, 3 and 4 and left row 2 alone, so flipping it introduces no disagreement.
audit.corrected: phases[2].side and win[2] flipped to Sett together, rating raised to 6/10, and the phase why rewritten around the real Mist rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appeared on the page — 'fight when Mist is down' with no idea how long that is.
audit.why: Hallowed Mist is 22/21/20/19/18s, Skip 'n Slash 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s (and partially refunded when she hits something), Needlework 120/100/80s. Mist's 22s at rank 1 against Facebreaker's 16s is the whole early-lane rhythm.
audit.corrected: Mist's 22s at rank 1 and 18s at rank 5 keyed to the level 3-5 and first-item spikes; Skip 'n Slash's 11s and R's 120s keyed to the level-6 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) The page tells the player to 'pull her out of her W Hallowed Mist bubble' — Riot's text says the opposite of what that implies: the mist protects her from enemies OUTSIDE it, and she can only be targeted by enemies who ENTER it. The instruction is step in, not pull out. (b) 'Q slow' again — Knuckle Down has no slow. (c) Facebreaker is called a stun with no mention that a lone target on one side is only slowed.
audit.why: Riot's Gwen W text: 'She summons mist that protects her from enemies outside of it. She can only be targeted by enemies who enter the mist.' Riot's Sett Q text has no slow clause. Riot's Sett E text: 'If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' The mirror called the Facebreaker condition the highest-value fact in this matchup and recorded it absent from both layers.
audit.corrected: The Mist instruction inverted to 'step in and she is targetable again' in spikes[0], mid, wants.you[2] and phases[2].why; the phantom Q slow removed; the across-the-minions condition on Facebreaker written into early and spikes[0]. Also noted: Snip Snip! deals true damage down its centre, so the page's 'build MR' headline is only half the answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemization line already recommends Executioner's Calling but says 'his healing out-paces your grit trades' — wrong pronoun for Gwen, and the anti-heal reason never reaches the content layer where the player actually reads about first-item trades.
audit.why: A Thousand Cuts heals her for a portion of the damage it deals to champions, on every attack — that is exactly the sustain that beats Sett's chip pattern.
audit.corrected: Pronoun fixed and Grievous Wounds moved into the first-item spike where the trade advice lives.

edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + Health Potion. Core: Stridebreaker (stick to her through the W panel window), then Sterak's Gage; boots Mercury's Treads. First back: Executioner's Calling (≈800g) — her passive healing out-paces your grit trades.

notes: The single biggest fix: the page told the player to pull Gwen OUT of Hallowed Mist, when Riot's text says the mist protects her from enemies outside it and she can only be targeted by enemies who enter it. Stepping in is the play; staying out is what makes her untouchable. Two things I did not assert. First, whether Facebreaker's area pull can grab her from outside the mist is not answerable from Riot's text — I wrote the advice as 'step in', which is correct either way, rather than guessing. Second, the mirror flagged that Sett's kit file carries a 'grounding' flag on The Show Stopper that Riot's description does not support; I asserted nothing about grounding, which matters here because Skip 'n Slash is her escape. The full-layer headline still reads 'build MR' — worth revisiting, since Snip Snip! deals true damage in its centre and A Thousand Cuts scales on the target's health, so MR is only a partial answer and stacking HP is actively bad.
